clue.text: Confirmation pleasure's no good?

indicators.note: 'no good' asks for the pleasure word with its abbreviation for good taken away

parts.note: gratification is a word for pleasure or satisfaction

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether getting official approval is no fun at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing G from GRATIFICATION leaves the answer; the question mark flags the playful reading of 'no good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratification is the formal approval of a treaty or agreement, a synonym for confirmation.

clue.text: Quietly sneaked into saint's memorial, a copy

indicators.note: sneaking into something means going inside it, so one piece is put within another

parts.note: a relic is a remnant of a saint kept as a memorial
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Someone slipped quietly into a saint's shrine to make a reproduction.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction, a synonym for copy.

clue.text: Checks jokes, having time for intro

indicators.note: time taking the place of the intro means the first letter of the jokes word is replaced

parts.note: jests are jokes

explanation.surface: Someone vets the gags, swapping in a new opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Tests and checks are both examinations to see if something works or is correct.

clue.text: Baby left in establishment

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the establishment word

parts.note: founding is the establishment of something

explanation.surface: An infant abandoned at an institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundling is an abandoned baby found and cared for by others.

clue.text: Talk about bowler, say

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
a bowler is an example of a hat

explanation.surface: Discussion about a cricket bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket but is the round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat is to talk informally.

clue.text: Restrained and looking embarrassed after breaking teeth

indicators.note: after places the embarrassed word behind the anagram
teeth that are breaking are smashed apart, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red

explanation.surface: Someone tied up and blushing after a dental injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethered means tied up or held back, so restrained.

clue.text: Love and admire discourse

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
to rate someone is to admire them

explanation.surface: Affection and respect for a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech; discourse is used here as a verb.

clue.text: Spoke badly of head of Mafia dealing crookedly

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
something done crookedly is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Mafia boss is smeared for doing dishonest business.
explanation.definitionFit: To malign someone is to slander or speak ill of them.

clue.text: Gambolled or gambled on

definitions.meaning: frolicked or romped, as children do
staked money on, as one does at the tables

explanation.surface: A choice between skipping about and betting.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both frolicking and wagering, nearly identical words in the clue.

clue.text: Candidate for admission put on last in error

indicators.note: letters set down in error are jumbled, signalling a rearrangement of the preceding words

explanation.surface: An applicant's name was mistakenly placed at the bottom of the list.
explanation.definitionFit: A postulant is someone seeking admission, especially to a religious order, so a candidate for entry.

clue.text: Use a cover for the audience

indicators.note: what an audience hears is spoken, so the letters are a sound-alike

parts.note: a veil is a cover for the face

explanation.surface: A sheet is used to screen something from spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means benefit or use, as in 'to no avail'.

clue.text: Sort of job behind bars?

definitions.meaning: a crime committed with help from someone within the organisation
a prisoner is said to be ..., meaning locked up in jail

explanation.surface: A crime that ends up with someone in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a crime aided from within and being locked up in jail.

clue.text: Famous person's heartless haste

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is cut out

parts.note: a celebrity is a famous person

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted star rushing about.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of CELEBRITY is its central letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for swiftness of movement, a synonym for haste.

clue.text: A source of friction — just business

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: fair means just or even-handed

explanation.surface: A cause of conflict that is purely a commercial matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or concern, as in 'that's my business' or 'that's my affair'.

clue.text: Going to get attractive?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one is about to become good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both retrieving something and being pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Experienced a bit of abuse, as one does

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, the letters run across them

explanation.surface: Someone has suffered some mistreatment, as people commonly do.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned describes a veteran who has gained experience over time.

clue.text: Short busy worker on bottom of ladder is of no importance

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece on another sits above it

parts.note: small means short in stature
a bee is a busy worker insect

indicators.note: the bottom of a down word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A little industrious worker at the foot of a ladder is insignificant.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer is an idiom for something trivial or unimportant.

clue.text: Panel of women popular within racecourse

indicators.note: within places the popular word inside the racecourse

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A group of fashionable women at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire, England, famous for Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is wooden panelling on the lower part of a room's walls.

clue.text: At home and tense, big returns being essential

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: returns means the word for big is read backwards

parts.note: large means big

explanation.surface: Being nervous at home while big profits come in is vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral describes something necessary to make a whole complete, so fundamental.

clue.text: Immigrant losing right to get revenue

indicators.note: losing means the letter for right is dropped

parts.note: an incomer is someone who has moved into an area

explanation.surface: A newcomer earning money after losing their entitlements.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is money received, a synonym for revenue.

clue.text: Look one gets in a gaggle

definitions.meaning: 'take a ...' is a slang expression for having a look
a male goose is found in a flock of geese, a gaggle

explanation.surface: A glance at something found among a group of geese.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a slang term for a glance and the name of a male goose.

clue.text: Decide to work out the answer again

definitions.meaning: to make up one's mind firmly

definitions.text: to work out the answer again
definitions.meaning: read as ..., to solve a second time

explanation.surface: A determination to redo a calculation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to determine and, split up, to solve once more.

clue.text: It's clear the man is protected by company lease

parts.note: he refers to a man
rent is to lease property

explanation.surface: A tenant is covered by a corporate rental agreement, and that's obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherent means logical and easily understood, so clear.

clue.text: A step up from manager is error

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: A promotion beyond management is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is the vertical part of a stair step, so the step up between treads.

clue.text: Puts steps across lake

indicators.note: steps going across the lake means the word for steps spans and encloses the lake's letter

parts.note: paces are steps
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone sets stepping stones over a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something is to put or set it down; both are verbs in the third person.

clue.text: Feature running across a mountain range

definitions.meaning: something stretched across, like one across a doorway or road
a ... of mountains is a range

explanation.surface: A landmark crossing a range of peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain is a linked line stretched across and also a line of mountains.

clue.text: Company doctor's groom

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: The firm's medic is a stable hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb is to groom hair, the verb sense of tidying up.

clue.text: Flash American's disadvantage

parts.note: a flash is a moment, a minute, abbreviated MIN
US means American

explanation.surface: An ostentatious American has a drawback.
explanation.definitionFit: A minus is a negative point or drawback, the opposite of a plus.

clue.text: Ring off — that's a lucky escape

definitions.meaning: to ring off is to end a telephone conversation, to close a call
a narrow escape from danger, a near miss

explanation.surface: Someone hangs up the phone, relieved to have got away with it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a cryptic reading of the phrase as a verb plus noun: shut the phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss or narrow escape from disaster is a well-known idiom for this phrase.

clue.text: Bit sticking out on pub terrace needs fixing

indicators.note: something that needs fixing must be put right, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A lump jutting out on a bar's patio ought to be repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: A protuberance is a bulge or projection that sticks out from a surface.
